subject: Platform fee coverage and support layering for ClearPulse deployment
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@clearpulse.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jake Moreno <jake.moreno@clearpulse.com>
Date: Mon, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions on platform fee + implementation surcharge

Hi Grace,

Thanks for sending the draft pricing and SOW. We're evaluating the commercials internally and have a couple of items we need clarified before we pull legal in for redlines:

- Platform fee: can you confirm whether the platform fee in your quote is applied per-site or per-account for a multi-region on-prem deployment?
- Implementation surcharge: it's listed as a one-time engineering surcharge. Is that waiverable with a 12+ month committed license? If not full waiver, can it be amortized into the platform fee over our term?
- Support tiers: we prefer 24x7 SRE coverage for production, but we'd like to understand the delta in response windows and the on-call retainer vs per-incident pricing.

We attached our internal procurement checklist and requested ratecard for reference. Can you point me at a clean breakdown (spreadsheet) showing platform fee vs operator license vs support retainer?

Also, timeline: procurement hopes to run through commercial approvals this week so if you can provide a short written concession path that would help accelerate.

Attachments: ClearPulse_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (pdf), Requested_Ratecard_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Amanda Li
Director, Procurement
ClearPulse
amanda.li@clearpulse.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@clearpulse.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial questions on platform fee + implementation surcharge

Amanda — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and a couple of optional concessions we can consider if ClearPulse is able to commit to a 12-month minimum.

1) Platform fee scope
- Our platform fee is quoted per-account (tenant) for multi-site / multi-region Private deployments. It covers the control plane, licensing for the serving runtime, telemetry/observability, and quarterly security reviews. Operator licenses are priced separately (per-operator seat or per-gpu node); see attached ratecard.

2) Implementation surcharge
- Standard practice: a one-time implementation surcharge (covers initial infra hardening, on-prem packaging, and project management).
- Concession option: waive the surcharge if ClearPulse signs a 12-month committed license at the proposed tier and accepts a 30% prepayment profile. Alternatively, we can amortize the surcharge into the monthly platform fee across the first 12 months (spread schedule included).

3) Support tiers
- Tier A (Standard): business hours support, 8x5, 4-hour P1 response SLA; Tier B (Premium): 24x7 SRE, 1-hour P1 response, includes on-call retainer and monthly incident review; Tier C (Enterprise): Premium + named SRE, quarterly runbooks, and extended observability retention.
- Pricing delta: Premium retainer is a fixed monthly fee (listed in the ratecard) plus per-incident credits for Sev2+/non-routine engineering. We can provide a worked example for ClearPulse workload.

Attachments: ClearPulse_Ratecard_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes amortization examples and Support tier matrix

If helpful, Ben can map the ratecard to your expected node counts and run a quick cost sensitivity. Irene is on the thread for any technical/ops clarifications and to confirm SOW language around responsibilities.

Proposed next steps: 1) I’ll share the amortized fee schedule and a version of the SOW with the waiver clause, 2) you confirm whether 12-month commit + 30% prepay is workable, 3) we exchange a DocuSign SOW.

Let me know if you want a short call this afternoon.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

Amanda — looping in to offer a practical concession and a quick cost example. Thanks for the checklist, that helped.

Concession proposal we can make today:
- Waive the one-time implementation surcharge in full if ClearPulse agrees to a 12-month committed platform license at the Tier B (Premium) level and a 25% prepayment (instead of the 30% Grace mentioned). This is a time-limited offer valid until May 12, 2027.
- If ClearPulse prefers monthly cashflow, we can amortize the surcharge across the first 12 months with a 5% uplift on the monthly platform fee to cover project management.

What I can do for transparency: two worked scenarios attached — (A) 12mo commit with surcharge waived and premium retainer; (B) month-to-month with amortized surcharge and Tier A support. Scenario A yields lower TCO over 12 months and keeps a SLA credit liability minimal.

Attachments referenced: ClearPulse_Ratecard_v3.xlsx (you should already have this) and a short SOW draft (ClearPulse_SOW_v2.pdf).

If that concession is acceptable, Grace and I will update the SOW with a clause noting the rebate/waiver conditions and add language for SLA credits (we propose a rolling cap tied to monthly usage to limit downside).

Ben Carter

Grace / Ben — thanks for the clear options and the worked scenarios. Procurement reviewed Scenario A and we can proceed with the 12-month commitment and Tier B Premium support if the following are confirmed in the SOW:

1) Implementation surcharge waiver is explicit and unconditional once the DocuSign SOW is executed and the 25% prepayment is received.
2) SLA credit cap: we accept a rolling cap equal to 10% of the monthly platform fee for P1 incidents, but request that P1 determination be jointly reviewed by ClearPulse and Redwood within 10 business days of an incident to avoid classification disputes.
3) Observability retention: extend retention to 90 days for debug traces (rather than the default 30) for the first 12 months — Redwood will include this as part of the Premium retainer at no additional charge as a one-time concession.

If you can return a redlined SOW that bulletizes the above three points and a DocuSign link, we'll route to legal and finance for signature. We're hopeful to get this signed by May 12.

Attachments: Signed_ClearPulse_Internal_Approval.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Amanda Li
